A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCP1 research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the additional material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, adversarial robustness, runtime, and Cityscapes risk-control experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original steering-angle regression results in Appendix E, Table 7.

M1.justification: The single-sample construction is retained, but its written calibration specification changes: Algorithm 1 uses Q(alpha') instead of v1's Q(alpha), and Section 2 revises Q's finite-sample definition. These are limited specification revisions; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates CIFAR-10/ImageNet classification and Cityscapes segmentation risk control. v2 retains these and adds Udacity steering-angle regression, substantially extending empirical coverage to continuous-output prediction. Regression was previously discussed theoretically.

E2.justification: BinCP remains the main comparator, and lip-rcp, VRCP-I, and VRCP-C remain in the small-radius comparisons. Changed BinCP sampling budgets are configurations of the same method. The new regression table introduces no comparator.

E3.justification: The regression experiment adds a protocol using ResNet18 fine-tuning for 200 epochs, Gaussian noise with sigma 0.5, 90% target coverage, and interval-width evaluation. The main CIFAR-10 comparison switches displayed BinCP budgets from 32/64/128/256 to 60/80/100/150; existing classification splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The sampling-budget sensitivity comparison is revised, including coverage and small-set proportions at different BinCP budgets in v2 Figure 7 versus v1 Figure 6. The adversarial attacks, TPS/APS comparison, smoothing comparison, and set-size variability analysis are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: The added checklist identifies Table 3 entries as mean plus/minus standard deviation and describes plotted error bars as confidence intervals, providing labels absent from v1. The stated 100 calibration runs and single risk-control run are unchanged; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical results. New Table 7 reports regression coverage/interval width of 0.900±0.005/0.371±0.012 at radius 0 and 0.963±0.003/0.667±0.026 at radius 0.50. Revised BinCP curves use different sampling budgets, so they do not establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Substantive revisions affect several central arguments. Proposition 1 removes v1's coverage step conditioned on all noise draws; Proposition 2 replaces radius restrictions with positivity assumptions and changes its lower-bound expression. The inverse-certificate proof is rewritten, while Section 3.2 corrects loss monotonicity and adds an admissible maximum-parameter condition.

C1.justification: The core single-pass efficiency, task-generality, and risk-control claims remain. v2 additionally claims the first randomized-smoothing certificate for conformal regression in Section 4 and Appendix E; v1 asserted regression applicability without this explicit novelty claim.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's assertion that convolution determines the robust coverage distribution with a conservative estimate of an unknown distribution. It also clarifies marginal versus noise-conditioned guarantees and expands the explanation of randomized versus deterministic prediction sets. The increased set-size variance limitation was already present.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub code link, a checklist statement about supplementary code, and regression implementation details including ResNet18, noise level, and training duration. Conversely, Appendix E drops v1's explicit statement that unspecified experiments use 90% nominal coverage.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Bojarski et al. for DAVE-2, He et al. for ResNet, and Romano et al. for adaptive coverage, alongside the regression novelty claim. Positioning relative to BinCP, CAS, and verifier/Lipschitz approaches remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, and theoretical narrative are extensively rewritten. v2 adds a high-level explanation, reorganizes the appendix discussions of guarantees and conservative calibration, and moves the algorithm into the main text. Acknowledgements and a conference checklist are also added.

P2.justification: v2 adds the explanatory Figure 2 and regression Table 7, presents a compact colored algorithm beside the new figure, and revises some plot axes and legends. Existing figures and tables are largely retained, with appendix rearrangement and table styling changes.

improvement.justification: The regression experiment supports an application previously claimed without empirical evaluation, and Proposition 1 removes faulty conditioning. The explanatory figure, accessible algorithm, and code link improve usability. These gains are limited by largely unchanged benchmark evidence and a problematic new Section 2 quantile definition: floor(alpha(1−1/n)) evaluates to zero for ordinary alpha, leaving the written calibration specification erroneous.
